reviews.title: Misleading Money-Back Guarantee
reviews.text:
The 30-day money-back guarantee is misleading if you subscribe through the App Store. When I requested a refund, I was told the guarantee only applies to purchases made directly through their website.

That restriction should be made clear before customers subscribe, not buried in the fine print. If you purchase through the App Store, don’t expect their advertised guarantee to protect you.

reviews.title: Money-back guarantee doesn't apply to App Store purchases
reviews.text:
The concept drew me in, and the advertised 30-day money-back guarantee is what made me comfortable subscribing without researching further.

After three guided sessions I'd had enough. The available guidance voices didn't work for me, and the content didn't feel well curated. I contacted support to use the guarantee.

I was told it only covers subscriptions bought directly through their website, not the App Store. That limitation is on their site, but it's buried in the text and I missed it, and buying through the App Store is the default path for most people.

Support declined to refund, declined to approve a refund on Apple's side, and declined to provide any documentation I could use in my request to Apple. The only response was to contact Apple myself.

If the guarantee is part of why you're signing up, buy through their website. Through the App Store, assume it doesn't cover you.

reviews.title: Hire Voice Actors & Sexual Healthcare Professionals
reviews.text:
I have an ethics problem with a tool that almost entirely is comprised of AI. They do not make that clear in advertisements, because I’m sure they realize that people with similar issues will not buy.

I think in theory this app could be very helpful. But when you replace voice actors with AI voices, include an AI chatbot giving “mental health/medical” advice with no discernible real human professionals being consulted for this information, it seems unethical at worst and lazy/corner cutting at best. 

Hire real voice actors and mental/sexual healthcare professionals who can be public facing and who can validate the advice being given , and you’d have a good tool worth the sticker price.
